_comment: Files where a request-controlled value reaches a filesystem path with no containment check detectable by scripts/ci/check-path-containment.mjs. Every entry needs a REASON. `sites` pins the exact text of each reviewed line: a new or edited site re-flags, so a baseline cannot quietly cover new code, while an unrelated edit elsewhere in the same file does not. This list may shrink, never grow.

server/routes/authoring.router.ts.reason: FALSE POSITIVE. `path.join(dir, file)` in loadTemplates(): `dir` is templatesDir() (a server constant, cwd/server/templates/m3) and `file` comes from fs.readdirSync on that directory, filtered to *.json. Neither is request input. The detector matches on the assignment target `content`, which is ALSO bound from req.body elsewhere in this ~4600-line router — a name collision, not a dataflow. (It previously matched on the name `file` for the same reason; the line itself is unchanged.) Re-verified by reading loadTemplates() and templatesDir() in full.

server/routes/protocol_routes.ts.reason: FALSE POSITIVE for THIS gate. `filePath` is `req.file.path` at every site — the path MULTER generated for the upload it just wrote, not a client-supplied string, so no request value reaches the path and there is nothing to contain. The client controls `originalname`, used only for path.extname. RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-19 after the two new sites appeared: they are the real PDF/DOCX extraction in POST /analyze-file replacing a hardcoded constant, reading the same multer-written path the .txt branch beside them already read — a new line, not a new source of path input. Both handlers read in full: POST /analyze-file binds filePath at :371 behind assertUploadSafe at :362, and POST /upload-and-optimize binds it at :713 behind assertUploadSafe at :704. (An earlier revision of this reason claimed that guard at both sites when only the first had it; the second has had it since.)

server/routes/analytics-routes.ts.reason: FALSE POSITIVE for THIS gate. `text` is the request BODY's protocol text and is the file's CONTENT, never its path: the path is `path.join(fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'protocol-')), 'protocol.txt')`, built entirely by the server. The detector matches on the name `text`, which is bound from req.body on the same line as the sink. Reviewed 2026-09-23, and in the same change the temp path was moved from a shared `<cwd>/temp/protocol-${Date.now()}.txt` (same-millisecond requests collided on one file) to a per-request mkdtemp directory. The handler (POST protocol text analysis) was read in full: the length bounds (50..100000 chars) precede the write, and both exits remove the directory.
